programme: FOXA1 (pioneer transcription factor; its target set includes the classic estrogen-response genes TFF1, GREB1 and AGR2) and NCOA3/SRC-3 (a steroid-receptor coactivator whose target set directly includes ESR1 and AR) form a nuclear-hormone-receptor coactivation node. DNMT1, the maintenance DNA methyltransferase, controls the methylation state that gates access to this layer, since pioneer factors such as FOXA1 characteristically read out methylated DNA directly.
role_in_a: In MS, FOXA1 is required downstream of neuronal IFN-beta/PI3K/Akt signalling to generate a FOXA1+ regulatory T-cell subset (PMID 28436428, 38117896), placing this pioneer factor inside the mechanism of an existing MS therapy (interferon-beta); NCOA3 has independently been nominated as a candidate familial-MS gene from exome sequencing (PMID 31170158), consistent with a nuclear-receptor-linked immunoregulatory node.
role_in_b: In PD, FOXA1 has a directly documented neuroprotective role via NF1 transcriptional activation (PMID 38143008), and DNMT1 is repeatedly reported reduced or dysregulated in PD blood and models (PMID 41101626, 39413738, 34153844, 33483902), consistent with loss of the methylation control that would normally restrain this pioneer-factor/coactivator layer.
shared_axis: Both diseases have well-established, oppositely sex-biased epidemiology with a hormonal component - MS is female-predominant with pregnancy-linked remission, PD is male-predominant with estrogen proposed as neuroprotective - so a FOXA1/NCOA3 hormone-receptor-coactivation axis, gated by DNMT1-dependent methylation, is a plausible shared molecular substrate that is read out differently per tissue: Treg differentiation in MS blood/immune cells, dopaminergic protection in PD brain.
reasoning: Each carrying factor is independently and specifically placed in at least one disease by retrieved papers, and FOXA1 is placed in both with mechanistically concrete roles, so this is not a bare co-occurrence. But no retrieved source ties FOXA1, NCOA3 and DNMT1 together as one axis, or states that MS and PD share it - the hormone-coactivation frame and the DNMT1-gating link are my synthesis across separately documented facts, not a retrieved claim.
support: PMID 38143008 - FOXA1 shown neuroprotective in a PD model via NF1 transcriptional activation. PMID 28436428 - neuronal IFN-beta-induced PI3K/Akt-FOXA1 signalling required to generate FOXA1+ Treg cells, an MS-relevant subset. PMID 38117896 - FOXA1+ regulatory T cell differentiation shown to depend on PRKAG2.2-linked metabolic signalling. PMID 31170158 - NCOA3 identified as a candidate gene in familial multiple sclerosis by exome sequencing. PMID 41101626 - DNMT1 levels decreased in PD blood cells. PMID 39413738 - DNMT1-linked promoter methylation pathway (via MALAT1/SOCS3) affects PD progression. PMID 34153844 - DNMT1-related pathway implicated in dopaminergic neuroprotection in a PD model. PMID 33483902 - DNMT1 dysregulated in PD via miR-17.
how_to_falsify: Run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for FOXA1 and NCOA3 in MS patient-derived Tregs and in a PD-model dopaminergic neuron system: if the two factors do not co-occupy shared hormone-response elements in either cell type, the coactivation axis is not operative. Separately, knock down DNMT1 in each system and test whether FOXA1 occupancy or FOXA1-dependent output changes (Treg differentiation markers for MS, NF1-target expression for PD) - if DNMT1 loss has no effect on FOXA1 activity in either system, the proposed methylation-gating link is wrong.
caveats: Blood (MS) vs brain (PD) tissue pairing means this is a cross-tissue mechanistic parallel, not a shared-tissue observation. 234 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs back the concordance counts, but target-set agreement across patient subgroups is a statement about network-inference stability, not disease mechanism. HOXB13, HOXB3, HOXB7, PAX8, WT1, ONECUT1, HAND1, FOXA2 and NR1I3 recur at comparable or higher rates (up to 227/234 for HOXB13) but are excluded as carrying factors: most have no Open Targets association or literature in either disease at all, and HOXB3/PAX8, though individually evidenced (HOXB3 as an MS CSF biomarker, PMID 33352356/29873030; PAX8 in PD blood methylation, PMID 33981329), do not mechanistically integrate into the hormone-coactivation story and are left out rather than forced in. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed canonical immune master regulators (IKZF1, RELB, STAT5A, RUNX2) before ranking, and the single-view exclusions removed factors (FOS, ETS2, RELA, NOTCH1, BATF3, CEBPB/G, KLF7, EZH2) that would have supported a generic inflammatory account - this analysis deliberately does not fall back on either.
